gap: No result ChatGPT got states Fluance's own cartridge limits: the RT81 and RT81+ arms take only 3.5–6.5 g half-inch cartridges 17 mm tall, can use the Ortofon 2M Red but not the 2M Blue, and the RT81's discontinued AT95E has a maker-approved upgrade to the AT-VM95.
standout_why: I compared against platterandplinth.com (says the RT81's AT95E/ATN95E are discontinued but gives no way forward), valveandvinyl.com (gives the RT81's AT95E only and says it doesn't state upgrade or stylus replacement), stylusandsound.com (RT81+ ships a VM95E but it doesn't say which replacement styli fit) and fewbetter.com (no turntable content when opened). Three of them already say the AT-LP70X takes the VM95-series styli, so that is not new. None gives the Fluance arm's cartridge weight and height limits, the 2M Red yes / 2M Blue no rule, the different vertical tracking angles (RT81 20°, RT81+ 23°), or Fluance's statement that the RT81 can be moved to an AT-VM95.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's 'RT81+ for hi-fi upgrades' over the RT81. For $50 more ($349.99 vs $299.99 on fluance.com today) the RT81+ already ships the VM95E, which takes all five VM95 styli that Fluance lists (C, E, EN, ML, SH). The RT81 ships the AT95E, whose replacement stylus platterandplinth.com reports as discontinued, so keeping it going means buying a whole AT-VM95 cartridge. On either deck, an Ortofon upgrade stops at the 2M Red.
